source: NCERT Class X, India and the Contemporary World II, History Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Pre-modern World and Trade
points: The world has been **connected** for centuries through trade, migration and the movement of goods, people, ideas and diseases.
The **Silk Routes** linked Asia with Europe and North Africa — carrying silk, spices, precious metals and ideas/religions.
**Food travelled:** foods like **potatoes, maize, tomatoes, chillies** came from the **Americas** after Columbus (**Columbian exchange**); diseases like **smallpox** devastated Native Americans.

sections.heading: 2. The Nineteenth-Century Global Economy
points: Three flows connected the world: **trade (goods), labour (migration), and capital (investment)**.
Britain's **Corn Laws** were abolished → cheap food imports; **indentured labour** (from India — 'girmitiyas') sent to plantations (Caribbean, Fiji, Mauritius) — a 'new system of slavery'.
**Rinderpest** (a cattle plague) in **Africa (1890s)** destroyed cattle → helped Europeans control African labour/land.

sections.heading: 3. World Wars and Depression
points: **World War I** — an industrial, total war; huge loss; economic disruption.
The **Great Depression (1929)** — worldwide slump: falling prices, unemployment, agricultural collapse; India's exports/imports fell, peasants hit hard.
**World War II** — even more destructive.

sections.heading: 4. Post-War Reconstruction — Bretton Woods
points: The **Bretton Woods Conference (1944)** set up a framework for the post-war economy.
It created the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank (IBRD)** to ensure stability and fund reconstruction.
This began an era of growth and global trade; later **decolonisation** and the rise of newly independent nations reshaped the world.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Silk Routes connected Asia–Europe–Africa (goods, ideas, religion).
Columbian exchange: potatoes/maize/tomatoes/chillies from the Americas; smallpox devastated Native Americans.
19th c. flows: trade, labour (indentured 'girmitiyas'), capital; Corn Laws abolished (Britain).
Rinderpest hit African cattle (1890s); Great Depression = 1929.
Bretton Woods 1944 → IMF + World Bank.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Bretton Woods (1944)** created the **IMF and the World Bank**.
**Indentured labourers** from India were called **girmitiyas** ('new system of slavery').
**Rinderpest** was a **cattle plague** in Africa (1890s).
The **Great Depression** began in **1929**.
